input.rationale: Scoped source explanation of the timestamp-consumption discriminator: config.go:201-205 defines the lease in terms of contact, and raft.go:1032-1094 counts recent voter contact. An error-free rejection is contact; neither the heartbeat-specific fact nor this consumer asserts same-term approval. No stronger authority assertion is found at this boundary. Independent protection exists when ordinary/pipelined replication receives a newer-term reply: handleStaleTerm signals stepDown and the main thread sets Follower (s-stale, s-stepdown-consume). For a pending VerifyLeader, heartbeat Success=false is separately delivered as a negative vote, enabling the negative-verification step-down branch (s-heartbeat, s-notify-votes, s-vote-result, s-verify-result). These mechanisms explain the scoped consumption concern without proving prompt step-down for the proposed delayed-replication history. Network fast-path dispatch and separate heartbeat workers preserve the scheduling question rather than resolving it. No obligation or Evidence is created; no overall correctness or stale-read safety conclusion follows.

feedback.answered: Source review distinguishes connectivity evidence from authority approval at the lease consumer, and identifies conditional independent step-down mechanisms. The suspected timestamp strengthening is not supported by this consumer or its lease interface. Sources s-stepdown-consume and s-replication-loop answer the previously unread notification receiver and worker-exit structure; s-heartbeat-dispatch-shape, s-heartbeat-dispatch and s-heartbeat-handler answer the fast-path routing structure. They do not establish a scheduling bound or execute the proposed history. All three prior counterevidence statements are retained verbatim.

input.counterevidence_resolution: No previous counterevidence was removed: all three accepted protection statements remain verbatim. The prior unknowns were refined, not silently discharged. (1) The prompt-step-down contract question remains open beyond the inspected lease interface; s-lease-contract establishes only loss-of-contact semantics. (2) Sustained heartbeat replies with blocked ordinary replication remain an unexecuted history; s-heartbeat-dispatch-shape and s-heartbeat-dispatch establish distinct dispatch routes only. (3) The compound unknown about stepDown consumption, worker lifetime and transport behavior is partially answered: s-stepdown-consume shows receipt transitions to Follower; s-replication-loop shows replicate exit closes stopHeartbeat and CommitTimeout initiates ordinary attempts. s-heartbeat-dispatch and s-heartbeat-handler trace the fast-path call. These observations do not resolve transport timeout/connection semantics, scheduling bounds, or completion of in-flight RPCs; those remain explicit unknowns. (4) The exclusion of commit, linearizable-read and deployment claims remains in the rationale, importance and refined unknowns. The scoped explanation resolves only suspected strengthening of contact at the lease consumer, not these broader questions. For this corrected submission every accepted unknown is also retained verbatim as an umbrella research gap. The compound stepDown/worker/transport item is only partially answered by the cited structural reads; it is not marked resolved. No accepted counterevidence or unknown is removed.
